title: A transaction valid at submission fails txBAD_SEQ at apply
pattern: Core applies a ledger's classic phase before its Soroban phase and re-checks the source account, sequence number, signatures and sequence-age preconditions at apply (TransactionFrame::commonValid; OperationFrame::checkSignature with forApply). Here a classic transaction earlier in the same ledger bumps the source account's sequence number, so this Soroban transaction fails with txBAD_SEQ. Its fee is charged and its sequence number is not consumed (tx_changes_before is empty). Readers that assume txBAD_SEQ never reaches a ledger, or that every failed transaction consumed a sequence number, get this wrong.

hazards.placement: TransactionResult.txBAD_SEQ in a closed ledger: source sequence bumped earlier in the ledger

facts.says: The transaction fails with tx_bad_seq although it was valid when submitted.
The transaction that caused it is in the same ledger.
The sequence number is not consumed: no change before apply.
No operation was applied: the operation meta is empty.
The transaction source is the account changed earlier in the ledger.
The unused resource fee is refunded after apply (two changes on the fee source).
